title: The Math Trick That Quietly Doubles Money
description:
Compound interest looks boring until you actually run the numbers. Here's the simple rule that shows how fast it moves.

Educational content, not financial advice.

#shorts #financefacts #money

scenes.text: There's a simple trick that tells you how fast money doubles, and it's just one division problem.
It's called the rule of seventy two. Divide seventy two by your interest rate, and you get roughly how many years it takes to double.
At six percent a year, that's seventy two divided by six, or twelve years to double your money.
At two percent, it's thirty six years. The rate doesn't just matter a little, it changes the entire timeline.
The reason it works is that each year's growth also earns growth of its own, not just the original amount.
That compounding effect is exactly why starting earlier tends to matter more than the exact rate you get.
